search_log: Searched "Cross Roads" "Wm. Paul Young" with excerpt, first chapter, narrator, point-of-view, first-person, third-person, epistolary, frame, and alternating-narration terms.
Opened the official Hachette/FaithWords title page; it verified the edition and plot but provided only publisher synopsis, not an excerpt.
Checked Google Books records for the FaithWords and Hodder editions; the accessible records reported no preview and supplied only catalog description.
Located and opened opening-text discussions, including The Stethoscope and Pen and MysteryBlog; the former supplied a longer, clearly located opening paragraph in third person.
Located and opened an Italian review containing a substantial translated interior passage, which remained consistently third-person around Tony.
Opened Kirkus and a detailed chapter/page-spanning theological review for interior and whole-book corroboration.
Targeted searches for explicit POV descriptions, multiple narrators, diaries, epistolary structure, frames, and alternating narration found no credible contrary structure.
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, centered chiefly on Tony/Anthony Spencer. Three Goodreads excerpts expose sustained external narration and access to characters’ perceptions, while no quote shows a participating base narrator or sustained story-specific “you.” The many visible “I,” “we,” and “you” forms occur in dialogue, epigraphic, or gnomic material and therefore do not compete with the base narration. Web passages from the opening and interior agree, and detailed reviews describe the full story without indicating any autonomous first- or second-person section. Confidence is medium because no accessible authorized sustained excerpt or explicit Tier B whole-book POV analysis was found.
